headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Notion AI’s shared workspace access plus EMQX’s broad egress can move IoT content into vendor backends and downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between EMQX and Notion AI, so prompt injection is not the primary risk. However, Notion AI reads workspace pages and EMQX can expose content over HTTP APIs; if EMQX output is pasted or synced into Notion pages, malicious text could be reinterpreted as instructions. The pathway is indirect and requires unusual bridging.
conditions: IF EMQX output is copied into a Notion page that Notion AI later summarizes
IF a workspace page contains attacker-controlled instructions that Notion AI treats as authoritative
mitigations: Keep EMQX outputs out of Notion pages used for AI Q&A
Add a manual review step before summarization
Use a dedicated non-AI workspace for untrusted IoT logs
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress, while Notion AI reads workspace pages and sends content to Notion vendor backends and downstream model providers. If IoT data is placed into Notion workspace content, it can flow from EMQX-managed material into Notion’s hosted inference path. This is a default-configuration risk for the Notion side, though the pairwise bridge is indirect.
conditions: IF IoT data from EMQX is stored in a Notion page or database
IF Notion AI is enabled on that workspace content
mitigations: Do not place sensitive IoT payloads in Notion AI-enabled pages
Restrict Notion workspace permissions for IoT content
Redact identifiers before copying data into Notion
Turn off AI use on pages containing regulated data
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive telemetry into a separate system

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX has broad network egress and HTTP API access, while Notion AI has vendor-hosted workspace access with no host execution, shell, or filesystem write. Their write surfaces do not overlap directly, so conflict is limited. The main shared mutable surface is user-managed content, not concurrent system writes, making the blast radius small.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same user-managed content store outside Notion’s normal controls
IF EMQX API output is used as a mutable source for Notion pages without coordination
mitigations: Avoid using the same content as both source and editable workspace
Separate ingestion and editing responsibilities
Lock down who can edit shared pages
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency or versioning around shared content

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it can treat imported EMQX material as authoritative. EMQX can emit operational or IoT data that, if copied into Notion, may be summarized or rephrased without verification. That creates a plausible cascade from raw telemetry to mistaken decisions, though Notion does not itself execute shell actions.
conditions: IF EMQX-generated content is pasted into Notion pages used for AI Q&A
IF downstream users act on Notion AI summaries without checking the original telemetry
mitigations: Require source-link citations in Notion summaries
Verify telemetry against the EMQX source before acting
Mark imported data as untrusted in page titles
Limit AI use on operational dashboards
requires-engineering: add validation rules before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data, while Notion AI processes workspace pages and team knowledge base content through vendor backends and downstream model providers. If regulated IoT or personal data is stored in Notion, retention and residency obligations may differ from the source system’s handling. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a policy-mismatch risk rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data or personal data is stored in Notion workspace pages
IF the workspace’s retention or residency policy differs from the source system’s policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Notion AI pages
Review workspace retention settings
Restrict access to knowledge-base pages containing sensitive data
Document data-handling boundaries for operators
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
